attributes.description: One bar per STEP, clustered side by side at each time bucket, ordered by when each step first fired so the cluster reads left-to-right in pipeline order. The order is derived from the data, never from a hardcoded step list, so a different workflow orders itself.
attributes.title: Step outcomes over time

attributes.description: Completed / Failed / Cancelled over the same selection, and WHICH STEPS produced each. The inner ring is the outcome, the outer the steps that reached it. Cancelled is coloured distinctly from Failed on purpose: a policy rejection and a defect send an operator to different places. READ ONE WORKFLOW AT A TIME. Every slice here is a share of the WHOLE selection, so with more than one workflow in range the percentages describe none of them: measured 2026-09-26, simple-abc sat at a healthy 50/50 while filefetcher-archiveexpander-chain was at 100/0 with its feed dead, and the blended pie read 67/33 -- a number that looks mildly off rather than like one workflow failing completely. The Workflow control above opens on a single workflow for that reason; widening it to several is a deliberate act and the percentages stop meaning what the labels say.
attributes.title: Outcome distribution
Run edges — entry dispatches and terminal outcomes
attributes.description: Where does the work enter and leave? For the fires that ENTERED in the selected range: inner ring entry (one record per entry-step dispatch) and terminal (one per outcome of a step with no successors, whatever its result); outer ring the step. Entry far above terminal is work that left the path between the edges (failures routed elsewhere, cancellations) or is still running -- the Step outcomes panels show where. With every poll drained, entry with no terminal is a quiet window, not a stall. The Step and Outcome dashboard controls do NOT apply to this panel: they filter out the dispatch record, which carries no Result and belongs to the entry step only, so they empty or skew the pie. The workflow control scopes it.

query.esql:
FROM logs-generic.otel-default
| WHERE attributes.StepRole IS NOT NULL
| EVAL entered = CASE(attributes.StepRole == "entry", 1, 0)
| INLINE STATS fire_entered = MAX(entered) BY attributes.CorrelationId
| WHERE fire_entered == 1
| STATS records = COUNT(*) BY attributes.StepRole, attributes.StepName

attributes.description: One row per (workflow, step, queue, message type, outcome) for every refused message. The Outcome column is TWO LABELLED BUCKETS rather than the raw log template, because the template's discriminating words sit at the END of a 60-to-150 character string and the column truncated them -- a parked row and a redelivered one rendered as the identical 'refusing message of type {Type} o', which is the one distinction this column exists to make. Parked means the broker was told and the message IS in that queue's .dead counterpart, recoverable by hand; NOT parked means the channel died before the broker heard the rejection, so it will be REDELIVERED and there is nothing in a dead-letter queue to find. They are one code branch, one metric bucket and one severity, so this column is the only place they are distinguishable. The split matches on body.text, which is match_only_text and so supports the phrase query -- the attributes.* fields are all keyword and a match against them returns zero silently.

filters.label: Parked - recoverable from the queue's .dead counterpart
NOT parked - redelivered, nothing in the DLQ to find

attributes.title: Refused messages - what was lost, and whether it reached a dead-letter queue
